correctness.rationale: A derivation of k[t]/t^N has form D_f=f(t)d/dt with f∈t^ℓk[t]/t^N, ℓ=0 when p|N and ℓ=1 otherwise, because 0=D(t^N)=N t^{N−1}f. For nonzero f=t^v u with u unit and g=u h, [D_f,D_g] corresponds exactly to u²t^(v−1)(t h'−v h), and each distinct j coefficient (j−v)h_j lives at degree j+v−1, so the centralizer basis and c_N(v) follow even at v=j=0 with zero coefficient. Number of f at valuation v is (q−1)q^(N−v−1). Summing q^c yields the complete nullity polynomial and commuting-pair count; for N=kp the residue decomposition v=ap+b produces the closed S_p(q). In char2, bases A_j=D_{t^{2j}},B_j=D_{t^{2j+1}} for N=2r and A'_j=D_{t^{2j+2}},B'_j=D_{t^{2j+1}} for N=2r+1 obey the same [B_i,A_j]=A_{i+j} truncated bracket, giving both Lie isomorphisms with the affine algebra of k[z]/z^r. Image of ad_(a,b) is ideal (a,b) and has rank r−min(v(a),v(b)); this independently yields the full common spectrum and exact pair count. Direct finite field adjoint matrix rank enumeration for primes p=2,3,5, truncations N=2..7 matches the c_N(v) and p|N pair count, corroborating the universal proof.

value.rationale: Adjoint-centralizer dimension distributions and commuting-pair probabilities are natural finite Lie-algebra invariants. A complete all-length formula together with a characteristic-two parity isomorphism explains a non-obvious structural equality between derivation algebras of different associative rings. It also isolates the known Witt special case rather than recomputing it as the result.

limitations: Ordinary one-variable derivation Lie algebra, not higher-variable Jacobson–Witt algebras or restricted-Lie operations.
Only the char2 pair N=2r and 2r+1 is asserted to be isomorphic; underlying associative rings are not.
